title: How an Air Compressor Works in 60 Seconds 💨⚙️ #shorts
description:
A small shop compressor can pack air into its tank at around 150 PSI, about ten times normal air pressure. A motor drives a piston that pulls air in, squeezes it, and pushes it through a one-way valve into the tank. A pressure switch turns the motor off at the limit and back on when the pressure drops. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#aircompressor #engineering #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: A small air compressor can pack air to *150 PSI*, about ten times normal air pressure.

steps.label: Motor
steps.text: An electric motor spins a *crankshaft*, driving a piston up and down in a cylinder.

steps.label: Intake
steps.text: As the piston drops, an *intake valve* opens and fresh air rushes in.

steps.label: Squeeze
steps.text: As it rises, the air is *squeezed* and heats up, then pushed through a one-way *check valve*.

steps.label: Tank
steps.text: The *tank* stores that air, and the pressure climbs with every stroke.

steps.label: Switch
steps.text: At the limit, a *pressure switch* stops the motor, then restarts it when the pressure drops.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Suck, squeeze, *store*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
